target_customer: App developers needing cross-device data sync, plus consumers using Simplenote
problem: Developers had to build their own sync backend to keep app data consistent across devices. Simperium offered a hosted sync service, shown off by the Simplenote notes app.
business_model: usage-based developer sync platform plus a free consumer notes app with a paid tier
product_category: cross-platform data sync platform and notes app

founders.name: Fred Cheng
founders.background_notes: The only founder on the YC page. Per a Lifehacker piece summarized in search, the pair began Simplenote in 2008 as a way to learn iPhone development.

founders.name: Mike Johnston
founders.background_notes: Named as founder by TechCrunch (2013); not on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: A real-time multi-device sync engine with conflict resolution, built on Google App Engine and handling millions of daily requests, which is hard for a two-person team.

defensibility.rationale: Once an app built on the sync API, switching was costly, and Simplenote had a loyal user base. Hosted backends from Parse and others competed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Automattic acquired Simperium and Simplenote in January 2013; Simplenote was relaunched in September 2013.

market_need_then: Mobile apps were multiplying in 2010 and 2011 and sync was a common developer pain; Simplenote already had about 750,000 registered users by January 2013 per TechCrunch.

branding.domain_note: Matt Mullenweg helped buy simplenote.com from a domain squatter during the Automattic deal in 2013, per TechCrunch.

identity.voice_and_tone: Simple and developer friendly; Mullenweg called Simplenote the coolest notes service around.

branding.brand_signature: Simplenote, a minimalist notes app that outshone its parent company's name
branding.community_and_virality: Simplenote has a loyal user base and third-party app integrations such as nvAlt; the shutdown of the old Simperium site was met with user outcry before Automattic's relaunch. Mullenweg publicly praised it in 2013.

brand_strength.rationale: Simplenote had a devoted following and a one-line name that explained itself, while the Simperium developer brand was hard to spell and less known.

outcome_analysis: Simperium grew out of the Simplenote app and sync engine that the founders built in 2008, raised a 450 thousand dollar seed in 2011 and reached about 750,000 registered users. Automattic bought the team and both products in January 2013, with terms undisclosed, and relaunched Simplenote in September 2013. The product still exists under Automattic, so this was a quiet but real success driven by a sticky consumer app.
notes: Seed of 450K appears in TechCrunch (Jan 2013) and one aggregator (ToolRadar, attributed to Simplenote). Whether more rounds exist was not found, so coverage is partial. Competitors named in a 2012 BaaS overview (CloudMine, Kinvey, Parse) are dated two years after the batch, so the list is empty. Founder education and prior employers were not found. Simperium launched August 2010 out of YC per TechCrunch. The mention of a relaunch in September 2013 comes from search coverage and Matt Mullenweg's 2013 post titles, not a fetched page. simperium.com is live and owned by Automattic.
